citation: E. F. May, J. Y. Guo, J. H. Oakley, T. J. Hughes, B. F. Graham, K. N. Marsh, and S. H. Huang, Reference Quality Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium Data for the Binary Systems Methane + Ethane, + Propane, + Butane and, + 2-Methylpropane, at Temperatures from (203 to 273) K and Pressures to 9 MPa, J. Chem. Eng. Data 2015, 60(12), 3606-3620.
raw_snapshot_policy: The NIST JSON was inspected and hashed but is not redistributed because the archive page does not state a redistribution license. The normalized numerical facts, exact URL and SHA-256, pairing provenance, and deterministic extractor are retained. Ordinary validation is fully offline.

uncertainty_availability.pressure: Per-point 95% expanded uncertainty supplied in ThermoML and normalized from kPa to Pa.
uncertainty_availability.temperature: No numerical uncertainty value supplied in the selected ThermoML records.
uncertainty_availability.liquid_composition: No numerical uncertainty value supplied in the selected ThermoML records.
uncertainty_availability.vapor_composition: Per-point heavy-component 95% expanded uncertainty supplied in ThermoML; the complementary methane fraction has the same absolute uncertainty.

source_anomalies: The selected CH4+C3 ThermoML data include 273.48 K and 283.38 K points although the article title and abstract state a 203 to 273 K range. The 0.48 K excess is plausibly consistent with a rounded title range; 283.38 K is the material discrepancy. Both temperatures occur independently in paired pressure and vapor-composition observations, so neither is an extractor pairing artifact. Both points are retained rather than silently discarded.
